Rounding at the end keeps the answer accurate, and the denominator of 2 is the difference of squares that made rationalising possible. A quick decimal check of the original gives the same value.
questions.hint: Multiply by the conjugate, then divide.

questions.subject: ALGEBRA_I
questions.learningObjective: identify the irrational entry among roots
questions.stem: A poster lists four roots: the square root of 81, the cube root of 27, the square root of 40, and the square root of 121 over 4. Which entry is irrational?

options.text: The square root of 81, because 81 has more than two digits
options.misconception: believes multi-digit radicands are never perfect squares

options.text: The cube root of 27, because cube roots of composite numbers are irrational
options.misconception: believes composite radicands always give irrational cube roots

options.text: The square root of 121 over 4, because the radicand is a quotient
options.misconception: believes any quotient under a root stays irrational

options.text: The square root of 40, because 40 is not a perfect square

questions.explanation: The square root of 81 is 9, the cube root of 27 is 3, and the square root of 121 over 4 is 11 over 2, so those three are rational. Since 40 is not a perfect square, no fraction of integers squares to it, so its root is irrational. Judging by the look of the radicand is what leads to the wrong choices.
questions.hint: Evaluate each root exactly before deciding.

questions.subject: ALGEBRA_I
questions.learningObjective: round a root to the nearest tenth
questions.stem: A survey records a diagonal as the square root of 30 metres. Report that length rounded to the nearest tenth of a metre.
questions.explanation: Since 5.4 squared is 29.16 and 5.5 squared is 30.25, the root of 30 lies between those values and is closer to 5.5, which gives 5.5 to the nearest tenth. The exact root is irrational, so the tenths figure is an approximation. Squaring the two nearby tenths is the standard non-calculator check.
questions.hint: Test 5.4 and 5.5 by squaring them.

questions.subject: ALGEBRA_I
questions.learningObjective: diagnose a wrong conjugate multiplier
questions.stem: A student rationalises 1 over the quantity root 5 minus 2 by multiplying top and bottom by root 5 plus 2, but then writes the denominator as root 25 minus 4 instead of simplifying. Which statement is correct?

options.text: The work is right, because roots multiply by multiplying the outer terms first
options.misconception: misapplies the product pattern to a difference of squares

options.text: The product is 5 minus 4, which is 1, so the denominator should be simply 1
The denominator should stay as root 5 minus 2, since only the top changes
options.misconception: believes rationalising alters only the numerator

options.text: The denominator should be root 5 plus 2, since conjugates keep a root
options.misconception: believes a conjugate leaves a radical in the denominator

questions.explanation: The product of conjugates gives a difference of squares, so the root of 5 times the root of 5 is 5 and 2 squared is 4, leaving a denominator of 1. Writing the root of 25 leaves the expression unsimplified even though it equals the same value. Rationalising is complete once no root remains below.
questions.hint: Use the difference of squares and then simplify both squares.

questions.subject: ALGEBRA_I
questions.learningObjective: multiply radicals into a whole number
questions.stem: A product of two measurements is the square root of 45 times the square root of 5. Report the exact value of the product.
questions.explanation: Multiplying the radicands gives the root of 225, which is 15. The product rule works because both radicands are positive, and the result is a whole number because 225 is a perfect square. Squaring 15 confirms the value exactly.
questions.hint: Combine the radicands into one root first.

questions.subject: ALGEBRA_I
questions.learningObjective: explain the purpose of rationalising
questions.stem: A student notes that 2 over the square root of 5 and 2 root 5 over 5 have the same value and asks why rationalising is worth doing. Which reply is correct?

options.text: Rationalising is required so that the expression counts as irrational
options.misconception: believes rationalised form determines the class of the value

options.text: Rationalising changes the value into something closer to the exact answer
options.misconception: believes rationalising improves accuracy rather than form

options.text: A whole-number denominator makes division, comparison and checking easier by hand
Rationalising removes the root from the number entirely, making it rational
options.misconception: believes clearing a denominator rationalises the whole value

questions.explanation: Rationalising multiplies by a carefully chosen 1, so the value is unchanged, and the benefit is a denominator you can divide by or compare without a calculator. Accuracy is unaffected because the transformation is exact. The value keeps its own class, so an irrational number does not become rational by moving a root.
questions.hint: Ask what changes when the denominator becomes a whole number.

questions.subject: ALGEBRA_I
questions.learningObjective: identify the simplest radical form
questions.stem: A worksheet asks for the simplest radical form of the square root of 75. Which of these four student answers is correct?

options.text: The square root of 25 plus the square root of 3, because roots split over addition
options.misconception: splits a root across a sum instead of a product

options.text: 3 root 5, because 75 factors into 3 times 25 and the smaller factor stays inside
options.misconception: places the non-square factor inside instead of outside

options.text: 15, because 75 is larger than 64 and so its root must exceed 8
options.misconception: believes the root of a large radicand exceeds its largest factor

options.text: 5 root 3, because 75 factors into 25 times 3

questions.explanation: The largest perfect square dividing 75 is 25, so the root of 75 is 5 root 3. Putting the square factor inside gives a different value, since 3 root 5 squared is 45 rather than 75. Squaring each candidate is the quickest way to confirm which is correct.
questions.hint: Find the largest perfect square that divides 75.

questions.learningObjective: evaluate a root of a decimal
questions.stem: A ramp grade is given as the square root of 0.49. Report the value of the grade as a decimal.
questions.explanation: Since 0.7 squared is 0.49, the square root of 0.49 is exactly 0.7. Writing 0.49 as 49 over 100 makes the split obvious, giving 7 over 10. The value is rational, so no approximation is needed.
questions.hint: Write the decimal as a fraction with a perfect square numerator.
